揮.meaning: A little old fisherman sees an <part>army</part> of seagulls swooping for his chips. He heaves his <part>anchor</part> over his head and swings it round like a lasso, roaring. The gulls turn back. Never doubt what a man will <kanji>brandish</kanji> for his chips.
揮.on: Then he waves his house <sound>key</sound> at them too, for good measure.
揮.kun: He shakes his <sound>foo</sound>t at a <sound>roo</sound>k that's still eyeing his fish.

惨.meaning: A snowman pays a <part>visit</part> to his cousin in the desert. By lunchtime he is a puddle with a carrot in it and a scarf on top, his <part>heartbeat</part> a tiny drip. He looks utterly <kanji>wretched</kanji>.
惨.on: His cousin, a cactus, offers him an ice cream <sound>sun</sound>dae to cool down.
惨.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat in a <sound>jee</sound>p tries to scoop him up with a <sound>me</sound>lon rind.

哀.meaning: A peacock loses every feather in a storm and turns up at the ball in a borrowed <part>garment</part>: a soggy tea towel. He opens his <part>mouth</part> to announce himself, and only a squeak comes out. Everyone pats his head. He looks <kanji>pathetic</kanji>.
哀.on: He tries to hide in a corner behind some <sound>i</sound>vy.
哀.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' sighs a duchess. '<sound>Wah</sound>,' sobs the peacock, into her <sound>re</sound>d hanky.

肩.meaning: A kind giant decides the <part>moon</part> looks lonely and needs a front door. He hoists a huge oak <part>door</part> up beside his ear and climbs a ladder of clouds all night, then fits it with a brass knocker. The whole trip, all that weight sat on one <kanji>shoulder</kanji>.
肩.on: Back home, his dog lifts its head out of its <sound>ken</sound>nel and wags.
肩.kun: He rubs his sore arm, <sound>ca</sound>lm again, and eats a cold <sound>ta</sound>co.

珍.meaning: A <part>king</part> holds a contest for the oddest pet. A <part>person</part> from the hills brings a goldfish with long curly <part>whiskers</part> that hums when you stroke them. The king trades his crown for it on the spot. Such a fish is <kanji>rare</kanji>.
珍.on: The fish strokes its whiskers like a wise old man stroking his <sound>chin</sound>.
珍.kun: In the palace it eats nothing but <sound>me</sound>lon, yu<sound>zu</sound> and <sound>ra</sound>men.

獣.meaning: In the <part>rice field</part> at night, a <part>dog</part> spots a <part>sparkle</part> of eyes and a huge <part>mouth</part> full of teeth. He barks bravely, then sees it's only a scarecrow with a kettle on its head and a moth on its nose. Still, he tells everyone he chased off a wild <kanji>animal</kanji>.
獣.on: The farmer gives him a shiny <sound>jew</sound>el collar as a medal.
獣.kun: The <sound>ke</sound>ttle clanks, the <sound>mo</sound>th flutters off, and the dog is <sound>no</sound>t so brave after all.

匠.meaning: An old woodcutter keeps his <part>axe</part> in a velvet-lined <part>drawer</part> and only takes it out for delicate work: a toothpick, a chess set, a violin from a single log. One careful swing, and a perfect wooden bird pops out. He is a true <kanji>artisan</kanji>.
匠.on: Every Sunday the whole town lines up to watch his carving <sound>show</sound>.
匠.kun: For the finale he carves a tiny <sound>ta</sound>rt, a <sound>coo</sound>k to bake it and a <sound>mee</sound>rkat to eat it.
